question: Explain Rutherford’s nuclear model of the atom. Hence discuss why the model could not completely explain the stability of atoms.

options.A: Rutherford’s model stated that positive charge is spread uniformly throughout the atom, so it fully explained atomic stability.
options.B: Rutherford’s model proposed a tiny massive positively charged nucleus containing nearly all atomic mass, with electrons revolving around it and most of the atom empty space. But a revolving electron is an accelerated charge and classical theory predicts it should radiate energy, lose energy, spiral into the nucleus, and make atoms unstable. Hence the model could not explain atomic stability.
options.C: Rutherford’s model stated that electrons are inside a neutral nucleus, so there is no electrostatic force.
options.D: The model fails because the nucleus has negative charge and repels electrons.
